analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 10.23.26
key_insights: Futures were stable pre-market (Nasdaq -10bps, S&P -35bps) with crude +1.5% (WTI above $100), after a sell-off the prior day in which semis fell 7%, AI-levered names 6% and AI data center names 8%.
GS HF Popular Pair Basket (GSTHVIPP) fell 4.2% the prior day, its worst move since 2011.

Overnight AI-related earnings were mostly better but drew mixed-to-lower stock reactions: WDC -4% pre (strong quarter and guide), BE -3% pre (beat and raise), FIX -3% pre (backlog +$3.8bn q/q, 'relentless demand'), MXL +3% pre (guided about 10% above the Street, up 15% q/q).

Per the GS PB team, Global Fundamental L/S managers, multi-strats and systematics all fell more than 1% on the same day, the first time since Covid. Investor performance challenges remain a major talking point.
SpaceX is reportedly in talks to access 80,000 cell sites for a fourth nationwide wireless network. AMT, SBAC and CCI rose 6-9% pre-market and T, TMUS and VZ fell 4-5%.
INFY fell 7% on lowered FY revenue guidance. RNG rose 16% on a raised FY revenue forecast.

WDC reported results and guidance well above the Street, but management implicitly acknowledged that competitors (GS believes Toshiba) could ramp units, and reiterated near-term capex modestly above its 4%-6% long-term range. GS expects the stock to trade modestly lower.

BE beat on 3Q adj EBITDA ($300mn vs Street $241mn), revenue ($1.24bn vs $1.08bn) and EPS ($0.94 vs $0.68 estimate), and raised FY26 revenue guidance to $4.4-4.6bn (Street $4.1bn), 122% y/y growth at the midpoint. The options market implied a 9% move.

Macro open: US 10-year yield higher at 4.98%. DRAM +2.5%, SMH +50bps, Hynix +4% pre-market. Asia closed mostly higher and Europe was lower on mixed PMIs. Kering fell 12% and Volvo Car 25% after results.

Oracle Investor Day is on 10/29. Since September 2025 Oracle has delivered FY26 revenue in line with its framework, raised its FY27 target to above $90bn, and grown RPO to $664bn from $455bn. GS expects updates on data center execution, demand sustainability and FY28-30 targets, and sees an inflection in OCI gross profit as the key company-specific dynamic over the next 12 months.

Micron's technology webinar on DRAM and NAND roadmaps points to expanding hybrid bonding and higher NAND layer counts. GS sees this as positive for Tokyo Electron (Buy), Disco (Buy), Ebara (Buy) and Kokusai Electric (Neutral).

China September IC import value rose 74.7% y/y (Aug +83.6%) on volume +1.7% y/y, implying IC import ASP +71.7% y/y. IC export value rose 136.0% y/y and IC production +24.2% y/y. GS says China semiconductor demand remains solid.

Spotify Q3'26: GS highlights strong premium subscriber growth, ad revenue trending toward double-digit growth, margin investments seen as transient with gross and operating margin progression expected in 2027, and the agentic media opportunity countering disintermediation fears.

Robert Half 3Q: Talent Solutions returned to positive growth (+2% y/y) for the first time since 2022, with 4Q guided to about +3% at the midpoint. Contract volumes remain negative and AI-related risk to white-collar staffing persists. GS maintains Sell.

QuantumScape 3Q26 non-GAAP EPS was -$0.14 vs -$0.17 for the Street and GSe. The new 100 MWh production line (start 2028) has no disclosed customer commitments. GS maintains Sell and assumes meaningful revenue starts in 2030.

market_movers.rationale: GS sees upside at current levels but expects the stock to trade modestly lower after results, and says HDD multiples are likely capped by long-run industry unit capacity increases.
GS prefers Seagate to WDC on a relative basis because of its stronger pricing momentum after navigating most of the HAMR technology transition.
Revenue returned to growth, but contract volumes are still negative and AI-related risk to white-collar staffing constrains the earnings recovery.
A long path to commercial volumes (meaningful revenue assumed from 2030), a challenging competitive landscape, and uncertainty around the VW PowerCo agreement.
Micron's hybrid bonding and higher NAND layer count roadmap is positive for Japanese semiconductor equipment makers.
Disco is rated Buy and benefits from the Micron roadmap update.
Ebara is rated Buy and benefits from the Micron roadmap update.
Kokusai Electric is rated Neutral and benefits from the Micron roadmap update.
Listed under Street Actions as upgraded to Neutral by JPMorgan.

sector_views.rationale: Demand remains solid. GS prefers names with company-specific drivers such as new product ramps, mix upgrades and share gains, supported by advanced node and generative AI.
Supply and demand are expected to stay constrained, but multiples are likely capped by potential long-run industry capacity increases.
Long-term AI risk to white-collar staffing and negative contract volumes constrain the earnings recovery.

earnings_insights: WDC: results and guidance well above the Street, stock -4% pre-market. Capex is guided modestly above the 4%-6% long-term range.
BE: 3Q reported adj EBITDA $300mn vs Street est $241mn. Revenue $1.24bn vs Street est $1.08bn. EPS $0.94 vs $0.68 estimate. FY26 revenue guide raised to $4.4-4.6bn vs Street est $4.1bn.
FIX: backlog +$3.8bn q/q reported, management cited 'relentless demand'.
MXL: guided about 10% above the Street, up 15% q/q.
QS: 3Q26 non-GAAP EPS reported -$0.14 vs Street and GSe est -$0.17. 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance reiterated at -$275mn to -$250mn vs Street and GS prior est -$263mn.
RHI: 3Q revenue largely in line with GS and consensus estimates, with upside to operating margins. Talent Solutions +2% y/y reported, 4Q guided to about +3% y/y at the midpoint.
SPOT: Q3'26 reported with strong premium subscriber growth and ad revenue trending toward double-digit growth.
INFY lowered FY revenue guidance and RNG raised its FY revenue forecast.
ORCL: Investor Day on 10/29. RPO is $664bn, up from $455bn, and the FY27 target is above $90bn.
Pre-market earnings on 10/23 include ALV, AXP, BAH and SLB.

tension_points.bull_case: AI-related earnings were mostly better, with beat-and-raise results from BE and strong guidance from WDC and MXL, and FIX cited 'relentless demand'.
tension_points.bear_case: Stocks reacted mixed-to-lower despite the good results, after a sharp sell-off in semis and AI-levered names and a record-bad day for hedge fund performance.

tension_points.bull_case: Management expects industry demand to stay strong and supply/demand to remain constrained for the foreseeable future.
tension_points.bear_case: Competitors, GS believes Toshiba, could ramp units, which would cap HDD stock multiples over the long run.
